strengths: One merge for the sync, a restore, the claim and the server copy, per field and commutative; nothing has a merge rule of its own (scripts/gm-store.mjs:306-326, 329-333).

A store's handle refuses every write on a client that is not a GM's, so no caller has to remember the check (scripts/gm-store.mjs:897-902).
A file's section is taken without its watermark, without another world's removals and with no stamp beyond the clock's bound (scripts/gm-store.mjs:531-549); a restore twice is a restore once.

The case summary is built by one pure allowlist: names and words only, links as indices of its own list, no node id, author or count of what is missing (scripts/case-summary.mjs:24-40); world-secrets.mjs holds the card to it (lines 251-256).

findings.title: Two counters that refute each other send the case map's layout into endless recursion; the Investigation panel then cannot open in its Map view on any GM's browser
findings.where: scripts/case-layout.mjs:103-105 (depthOf) and :90-92 (the cycle check reads input edges only); reached from scripts/investigation.mjs:1148 and scripts/case-trial.mjs:66
findings.what_happens: On the Map a counter's Refutes list offers every other node that is not evidence, other counters among them (investigation.mjs:1320, 1473-1475), and Save or any close writes the ticks through setCaseNode with no check for a loop (investigation.mjs:1584-1587; checkCase, case-schema.mjs:560-584, names none and blocks nothing). layoutCase refuses a cycle of input edges, but a counter with no input takes its depth from the nodes it refutes, by recursion, and a depth is remembered only once the recursion has returned. With A refuting B and B refuting A - or a counter refuting a deduction that lists that counter among its inputs - depthOf never returns and throws RangeError. caseMapRegion calls layoutCase while openInvestigationDashboard builds its body (investigation.mjs:2275-2284); every caller opens the view the GM's User remembers, and the default is the Map (investigation.mjs:1103-1106, 2268; gm-panel.mjs:262), so the panel throws before it has a window. The rows are a synced, backed-up GM store, so every GM's browser and the server copy hold the loop.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM ticks counter B under counter A's Refutes and counter A under counter B's, closes the Investigation panel, and from then on the Investigation tile answers that the action failed on every GM's browser, and the trial console's schema slot stays empty.
findings.expected: A loop is told on the Map and drawn around, as a cycle of inputs is: case-layout.mjs:8-10 ('A cycle of inputs has no depth, and the layout refuses it (`cycle`, the nodes on it) rather than drawing one: C8's consistency check says so to the GM') and case-schema.mjs:545 (warnings that block nothing).
findings.fix_sketch: Keep a visiting set in depthOf (a node met again reads depth 1), or hand cycleOf the refutes edges of the counters that have no input and name them under `cycle`.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a guard on the write road (applySchemaSave, setCaseNode, caseNodeOf: `refutes` is any list of ids), in graphOf (it keeps every refutes edge whose target exists, case-schema.mjs:342-345), in checkCase (no code for it) and around the callers (no try/catch at investigation.mjs:1148; the trial console's mount is caught at trial-floor-ui.mjs:1637-1638, so the console itself stands). Ran layoutCase from this checkout in Node on three hand-built graphs with graphOf's edge shapes (read-only; scratchpad layout-probe.mjs): two counters refuting each other and a deduction resting on the counter that refutes it both throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`; the control, a counter refuting a deduction, lays out. Looked for a way back in the interface: every caller opens the default view, the Table draws no schema editor, and Clear the plan would take the chapter's whole plan; `investigationView` can be set to "table" on the User only from the console.
findings.tests_near: R3375 (tier 0, scripts/tests-tier0.mjs:24285-24323) lays out a cycle of inputs (a rests on b, b on a) and holds `cycle`; no test builds a loop of refutes. R3376 (reachability) reads input edges only.
findings.live_check: On the Map add two counters, tick each under the other's Refutes, Save, open Investigation again: the panel should open and name the loop.

findings.title: Every read of the case's server copy runs Restore's preview, which clones a whole store once for each of its rows: 0.6 s at 600 answer keys and 2.5 s at 1200 (Node, built rows), on the primary before each debounced write and on every GM at load
findings.what_happens: case-copy.mjs reads each copy through restoreCase(file, { quiet: true, recheck: false }): at every GM's load (copyAtLoad) and, on the primary, as the first step of every write (writeServerCopy, line 177), which a change of any backed-up store's key schedules 15 s later, 60 s at most under steady change (44 of the table's 66 stores are backed up, by a count of the definitions). restoreCase computes previewSection for every store before it merges, quiet or not; a quiet read uses nothing of it but a count case-copy.mjs never reads. previewSection walks the file's keys and for each calls mergeSections(base, one), whose first line is a structuredClone of this browser's whole section. The merge that does the work is one pass. Measured here, read-only, on the checkout's gm-store.mjs in Node v22 (4 cores; scratchpad preview-cost.mjs, preview-cost2.mjs): answer-key-sized rows 300 / 600 / 1200 (100 / 200 / 400 KiB) take 126 / 644 / 2499 ms; trace-sized rows 500 / 1000 / 2000 with a fifth as many tombstones (336 / 673 / 1345 KiB) take 885 / 3385 / 17338 ms; the merge alone 19 / 39 / 114 ms.
findings.failure_scenario: Late in a season the primary GM's browser - the one that draws every player's roll and judges every request - stands still for a second or more about once a minute while the class plays, and at each load, with nothing on screen saying why.
findings.expected: case-copy.mjs:46-49 gives the debounce as the cost's bound ('each write lists, reads and uploads; fifteen seconds gathers such a burst into one'), and LIVE-E111-01 asks how long a read takes; the merge is one pass, and the preview is the Restore window's, where a GM waits for it once.
findings.fix_sketch: Do not compute the preview for a quiet read (or only when `beforeCut` asks for its keys); or make the per-key pass merge into a section holding that key alone.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that the preview is unconditional (gm-stores.mjs:2447-2476: no branch on `quiet` before line 2455), that the read comes before every write and not only the first (case-copy.mjs:176-178), that the debounced write is the primary's alone (case-copy.mjs:218) and what wakes it (clientSettingChanged of any `backup: true` key). Looked for a bound on a store's size: the bullets' and the traces' stores are cut by a season reset only, the balance log by none (gm-stores.mjs:1708-1711). Not established: how many rows a late-season world's stores hold - the numbers above are built rows, in Node, not a table's.
findings.tests_near: R7346 and R7348 (tier 1, scripts/tests-tier1.mjs:62559-62604) and scenario 34-case-seal hold what is read, merged and written, on stores of a few rows, and time nothing. LIVE-E111-01 (AUDIT 9.2 item 549) asks the time of a read and is open.
findings.live_check: On the primary of a late-season world: `f = await game.drpg.backupCase(); console.time('read'); await game.drpg.restoreCase(f, { quiet: true, recheck: false }); console.timeEnd('read')` (it saves the file too), beside `game.drpg.gmStoreStatus().perStore` for the rows and bytes behind the number.

findings.title: Since the server copy, the tombstone compaction does not hold for a backed-up store: each read of the copy merges the removed tombstones back, and counts as a restore that changed something
findings.where: scripts/gm-stores.mjs:1967-1980 (compactGmStores); scripts/gm-store.mjs:1070-1076 (compact: removed here, not sent) and :531-534 (fileSection keeps a same-world file's tombstones); scripts/case-copy.mjs:138-158; scripts/gm-stores.mjs:2473-2483
findings.what_happens: On each GM, once hydrated, compactGmStores removes the tombstones older than 30 days (TIMING.gmStoreTombstoneDays) whose subject is gone, in the stores that state `exists` (31 of the 44 backed-up ones), and counts on every holder running the same rule. The server copy is a holder that never runs it: the file is written from the sections, tombstones and all, and read back by restoreCase's merge at every load and before every write. Read after the compaction, the tombstones merge straight back; read before it, the primary's write 15 s later reads the file first, merges them back and then finds the file 'same'. The count of changed keys is not zero either way, so the quiet read is handled as one that took something: the tombstones go to the other GMs as a delta, the store's `afterRestore` sends every connected player their copies again, and the Faint pass runs - at each load, from the day a world holds such a tombstone.
findings.failure_scenario: From the 31st day after a Remnant or a Truth Bullet was deleted, every GM's load removes its tombstone and puts it back within a quarter of a minute, sends the players their bullets' refs (and the other copies) again, and the stores never get smaller.
findings.expected: gm-stores.mjs:1946-1966 (a tombstone of a gone subject goes after the bound) and gm-stores.mjs:2470-2472 ('A quiet read that took nothing ... sends no player anything and runs no Faint pass').
findings.fix_sketch: Apply the compaction's rule to a file's section before it is merged (and to the sections before a file is written), or have fileSection leave out the tombstones this browser's rule would remove.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that a tombstone put back counts as a change (mergeInto compares [e, t, d] of the key, gm-store.mjs:317-322; mergeIn answers the count), that fileSection empties `d` for another world's file only, that the file is not rewritten without them (the write compares the sections after the read merged the file back: case-copy.mjs:177-183), and the order of the three hydration hooks (module.mjs:430-433: health, copy, then the compaction registered by openGmStores) - either order ends with the tombstones back.
findings.tests_near: R7348 and scenario 34-case-seal read a copy over fresh rows; the compaction's tests (scripts/tests-tier1.mjs:19600-19635, scripts/tests-tier2.mjs:56470-56541) read no copy. Nothing crosses the two.
findings.live_check: In a world older than 30 days with deleted traces: `game.drpg.gmStoreStatus().perStore.map(s => [s.name, s.dead])` right after a load and a minute later - the counts come back to the first reading.

findings.title: When players are let into the file browser, the copy already on the server stays as it is, and the GM is told only that no copy is written
findings.where: scripts/case-copy.mjs:170-175, 203-207, 261-268; lang/en.json DRPG.Case.copy.refused.switchOff, .roles, .account (lang/pl.json the same); scripts/gm-stores.mjs:2679, 2896-2897
findings.what_happens: Once filesPrivate() answers a reason - the switch enforcePlayerFiles off, a Player or Trusted Player role or a player's account given FILES_BROWSE or FILES_UPLOAD - the module stops writing and reading the copy and says so: once a session on the primary's screen, in the case window's line and as a conflict row of the health check. The file written before stays in worlds/<id>/drpg-case under its name; nothing overwrites or empties it, and it is the whole case as Back up writes it. The stage's default for exactly this (Q-E111-5) is that the GM removes the old file by hand, but none of the three texts, the health row or the handbook's paragraph (gm-handbook.en.md:1415) says that a file is there, where it is, or that it is now within a player's reach.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM turns Keep players out of the file browser off so that players can upload portraits; a player opens the file picker, browses to worlds/<id>/drpg-case, opens case-<32 hex>.json and reads the killer, the Mastermind and every answer key, while the GM's notice said only that no copy is written.
findings.expected: docs/dev/e111/STATUS-115.md:72-74 (Q-E111-5: 'the file already written stays on the server. Default: tell and refuse from then on; the GM removes an old file by hand if a player could have listed it') - a GM can remove only what the notice names; the trust model's first rule (the rules file trust-model.md, line 15: a player's browser is trusted with nothing that belongs to somebody else).
findings.fix_sketch: Where a copy is known (`copyStatus().found`, or after a listing), add to the three texts and the health row that a copy is on the server in the world's drpg-case folder and has to be removed by hand; or upload an empty file over each known name before refusing.
findings.refutation_tried: Read every branch that follows a refusal (writeServerCopy, copyAtLoad, tellRefused, copyStatus, copyLineText, the health row): none touches the folder or names the file's existence. The module's side is read; that a player's account with FILES_BROWSE can list a folder under worlds/ and fetch the file is Foundry's, the stage's own premise and not read on 14.370 (LIVE-E111-02, AUDIT 9.2 item 550, open) - hence suspected. The protection by name and listing permission, with no encryption, is the owner's decision (case-copy.mjs:4-18) and is not the finding.
findings.tests_near: R7345 (tier 1, scripts/tests-tier1.mjs:62543) and scenario 34-case-seal B1-B2 hold that nothing is written while the files are open; nothing reads what the GM is told about a copy written before.
findings.live_check: LIVE-E111-02, then: write a copy, turn the switch off, and as a Trusted Player run `FilePicker.browse("data", "worlds/<id>/drpg-case")`.

findings.title: A second body announced while the first planned Autopsy is still going out is dropped, not queued: its planned Autopsy is not sent
findings.where: scripts/case-realize.mjs:257 (the guard), 259-262 (what is due is read once), 207-210 (the hook, not awaited)
findings.what_happens: The primary's listener of the body's announcement calls sendPlannedAutopsy and does not wait for it. The function reads what is due from the bodies found at that moment, then marks the chapter as sending while it issues each Autopsy to every living student, one item and one whisper a student (truth-bullets.mjs:1043-1072). A second stamp of the same chapter that arrives meanwhile finds the chapter in `sending` and returns 0; the first call walks only the list it read, and nothing calls the function again until another body is found. The second planned Autopsy stays planned.
findings.failure_scenario: In a chapter with two bodies the GM answers the two waiting discoveries one after the other; the first Autopsy reaches the class, the second, planned for the second body, never does, and the Map still shows it as planned.
findings.expected: case-realize.mjs:243-253: each planned Autopsy that is due goes out when its body is found, with no click of the GM's ('gracze dostaja od razu po odkryciu ciala. Bez kliku GMa'); `sending` is there so that two calls send once, not so that one is lost.

findings.refutation_tried: Read the announcement's road (body.mjs:476-494, 561-580): the listener hands no waitUntil, so the discovery does not wait for the sending, and a second discovery can be stamped while it runs. findings.title: Cancelling the browser's file dialog in Restore from a file leaves the tile's promise pending: the GM panel does not come back
findings.what_happens: Restore from a file (the case window's button, and the health window's) asks for a file through a detached <input type=file> and resolves only in its `change` listener. A file dialog that is dismissed fires `cancel` on the input and no `change`, so the promise never settles. The GM panel closes itself before a tile runs and reopens when the tile's promise resolves (gm-panel.mjs:579-593, 605-618): after a cancelled dialog `await item.run()` never returns and the panel stays closed. From the health window the same pending promise is what runHealthCheck returns.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM opens The case from the GM panel, presses Restore from a file, thinks better of it and presses Cancel in the browser's dialog: no window is left and the GM panel does not reopen, where every other tile brings it back.
findings.expected: gm-panel.mjs:579-593 ('Each tile closes the panel, does its thing, and the panel comes BACK'); chooseCaseFile's own comment ('null when none was picked', gm-stores.mjs:2940).
findings.fix_sketch: Resolve null on the input's `cancel` event as well.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a `cancel` listener or another settle of the promise (none in gm-stores.mjs; the only other resolve is inside `change`) and for a timeout around item.run() (none). The suite hands openRestoreDialog its text and never opens the dialog, so no test can see it. That a dismissed file dialog fires `cancel` and not `change` is the browsers' behaviour, not Foundry's; not run here.
findings.tests_near: none found: the tests of the restore pass `text` to openRestoreDialog.
findings.live_check: GM panel, The case, Restore from a file, Cancel in the browser's dialog: the panel should come back.

findings.title: While a health check has found something missing, every write of a backed-up store on the primary runs the whole check again, and the check reads and parses every store's key
findings.where: scripts/gm-stores.mjs:3041-3046 and 3027-3040 (the recheck); :2667 and :2721-2735 (gmStoreStatus inside gmStoreHealth); scripts/gm-store.mjs:1108-1120 (statusOf)
findings.what_happens: After a check that found a missing row and a GM's Continue, lastHealth.missing stays set for the session. From then on each clientSettingChanged of a backed-up store on the primary calls gmStoreHealth again (one at a time, one more when a change lands meanwhile): every scene's traces, every character's bullets, the secret projects, the notes, the traps, fillsFromTraces twice (lines 2518 and 2685), and gmStoreStatus, which asks each of the 66 handles for its status - a read of the store's whole key from localStorage and a JSON.parse of it, every world's section included - and then walks every key of the module's storage.
findings.failure_scenario: A primary GM who continued past one missing answer key pays a full scan of the world and a parse of every store on each room discovered, each trace placed and each roll logged for the rest of the session.
findings.expected: gm-stores.mjs:3020-3025: the recheck is there so that the red line goes when another GM's restore arrives; the bytes are an information row no red line reads.
findings.fix_sketch: Debounce the recheck, and leave gmStoreStatus out of it (or read the bytes only for the window and diagnostics).
findings.refutation_tried: Checked the guard (it stops only while nothing is missing, a window is open or this is not the primary) and that nothing coalesces the calls beyond the one running. The cost was not measured: it grows with the module's bytes in localStorage, which the health check itself reports.
findings.tests_near: none found: `grep -a -n "C-m15\|caseWarning" scripts/tests-tier*.mjs` answers nothing, so neither the recheck nor its cost is held by a test I could name.

findings.title: The case summary is marked sent before its card exists, and a card that was not created is still reported as sent
findings.what_happens: Send writes the trial record's summaryShown first and creates the public card second, and does not read what ChatMessage.create answers. When the create throws or answers nothing, the trial's record says the summary went out: a second press says it was already sent, and Replay finds no card. With a create that answers nothing the GM is also told 'Summary sent.'
findings.failure_scenario: The card's creation fails once (the socket drops at that moment, or another module's preCreateChatMessage turns the card down): the class gets no summary this trial and the console's button reads Summary sent.
findings.expected: case-summary.mjs:56-61: Send posts one public card and marks it sent, so that a second press sends nothing; the mark stands for a card.
findings.fix_sketch: Create the card first and write the mark when it exists; or take the mark back when no card came.
findings.refutation_tried: Read setTrialProgress's road for another GM (trial-progress.mjs:525-533: asked of the primary, written here when it does not answer) - the mark is written either way. Looked for a way to clear summaryShown inside a trial: only the trial's entry blanks it (trial-progress.mjs:380). The failing create itself is not something this code causes; no reading of one, hence suspected.
findings.tests_near: R3916 and scenario 63 S hold that a second press sends nothing; nothing fails the create.

by_decision.what: The server copy is protected by an unguessable name and by Foundry's listing permission, not by a passphrase or encryption; a name that leaks is the whole case.

A copy written before a player was given FILES_BROWSE stays on the server; the module tells and refuses from then on and the GM removes the old file by hand (the default taken; the texts' silence about it is finding 5).
Nothing in the copies' folder is ever deleted; two first writes that raced leave two files, both merged at every read.
The question at a body is the primary GM's alone and is asked once a chapter; a second body asks nothing.
The trial's ticks are a trial's: a second Class Trial in the chapter starts with none; the ticks are not in the case's backup.
The summary's evidence is every Remnant on the schema a student holds a copy of, the culprit included; deductions and counters only when a GM ticked them.
The case's consistency check warns and blocks nothing.
Back up asks its question in a second window after the case window's button.
A player's draft kept while no GM was online goes as it is when one connects, over a GM's edit made meanwhile.
In the trial console a press on a node, or on the fold of the unrelated evidence, opens and folds nothing: the schema is read only there.
The reset's keyPlan group, ticked, also cuts the case schema and the Logic Dive sets (each store's row says it is cut with the plan).
